cards.explanation: The answer is the first and the last. He says, "I am He; I am the first, and I am the last." (Isaiah 48:12) That's how He introduces Himself to Jacob and Israel, whom He has called. He tells them who He is before anything else.

The answer is that they stand up together. The verse says, "when I summon them, they stand up together." (Isaiah 48:13) That's the same hand that founded the earth and spread out the heavens, and now they answer it as one. No late ones, no stragglers, and no one hitting snooze. This is the same One who says, "I am the first, and I am the last." (Isaiah 48:12)

The answer is False. The LORD asks, "Which of the idols has foretold these things?" (Isaiah 48:14) The verse doesn't name any idol that did. Then in the next verse He says, "I, even I, have spoken…" (Isaiah 48:15)

The answer is Babylon, friends. "The LORD’s chosen ally will carry out His desire against Babylon, and His arm will be against the Chaldeans." (Isaiah 48:14) The Chaldeans are mentioned right alongside it. Both names come back in verse 20.

The answer is succeed. "I have brought him, and he will succeed in his mission." (Isaiah 48:15) The LORD says this about His chosen ally, the one who will carry out His desire against Babylon. He says it plainly, with no maybe in it. Right before that He says, "I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him." (Isaiah 48:15)
The answer is False, friends. "From the beginning I have not spoken in secret…" (Isaiah 48:16) He says it plainly, in the open. Nothing is hidden in the back of a drawer.

The answer is the Lord GOD. "And now the Lord GOD has sent me, accompanied by His Spirit." (Isaiah 48:16) The verse doesn't tell us who this speaker is, and I won't guess. What it does say is clear: the Lord GOD sent him, and His Spirit comes along. The sender is named right there in the verse.

The answer is that He directs them in the way to go. The LORD says He is the One "…who directs you in the way you should go." (Isaiah 48:17) He teaches and He directs. So He's not only handing out lessons, He's pointing at the road too.

The answer is peace in the first blank and righteousness in the second, friends. "If only you had paid attention to My commandments, your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like waves of the sea." (Isaiah 48:18) A river keeps flowing, and that's the picture He gives for their peace. Waves keep rolling in and never run out, and that's the picture for their righteousness. Two big pictures, one if only.

The answer is True. "Your descendants would have been as countless as the sand, and your offspring as numerous as its grains…" (Isaiah 48:19) That's more descendants than I have crumbs on my counter after a big batch. All of it belongs to that same if only. He's describing what could have been.

The answer is their name, friends. "their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence." (Isaiah 48:19) That's part of the same if only, right after the descendants as countless as the sand. Their offspring would be as numerous as its grains, and their name would still stand in His presence. A name that is never cut off is what He pictures.

The answer is True. "Leave Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! Declare it with a shout of joy…" (Isaiah 48:20) The command to leave and the call to declare it come back to back. A shout of joy is what the verse asks for.

The answer is redeemed in the first blank and Jacob in the second, friends. "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!" (Isaiah 48:20) That's the news the verse says to proclaim with a shout of joy, and to let it go out "…to the ends of the earth…" Good news travels faster than the smell of fresh cookies. Jacob is the name the LORD uses for His people in this passage (Isaiah 48:12), and He calls him His servant.

The answer is False. "They did not thirst when He led them through the deserts…" (Isaiah 48:21) The verse goes on, "He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and water gushed out." (Isaiah 48:21) So they weren't left thirsty. Desert, yes. Thirst, no.

The answer is the wicked, friends. "There is no peace," says the LORD, "for the wicked." (Isaiah 48:22) It's a short line and a heavy one. Back in verse 18 He pictured peace like a river, so this is a quiet stop.
